title: Fast post-quantum signature aggregation with lattice SNARKs - a16z crypto
gist: a16z crypto's Aerie aggregates Falcon lattice signatures with lattice SNARKs at over 50,000 signatures/sec on one laptop, ~29x faster than Ethereum's planned leanVM hash-based XMSS aggregation, and the authors argue hash-only post-quantum designs are more brittle and cannot support private payments without lattices.

insights.claim: Aerie aggregates 32,768 Falcon-512 signatures in 0.65 seconds on an Apple M4 Max laptop without GPU, over 50,000 signatures per second, versus the 1,000 per second targeted in the Lean Consensus team's 2026 plan.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: A single laptop can aggregate a full Ethereum slot of post-quantum signatures, removing a key scaling objection to PQ migration.

insights.claim: The aggregate costs about 42 bytes per signature, roughly 16x smaller than Falcon-512 signatures (666 bytes) and nearly 30x smaller than Falcon-1024 (1,280 bytes); a proof is about 66 KiB and verifies in 54 ms on one core, 10x faster than checking signatures one by one.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Aggregation neutralizes the 10-100x post-quantum signature bloat that would otherwise hit block size and node costs.

insights.claim: Versus Orthus, the fastest prior Falcon aggregation scheme, Aerie proves 1.5x faster, verifies 38x faster and produces proofs 1.7x smaller, and unlike prior work it also checks canonical signature encoding.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Prior lattice aggregation results were both slower and less faithful to the standard verifier.

insights.claim: Aerie aggregates about 50,800 signatures per second versus about 1,770 for leanVM on XMSS, and leanVM's stateless hash-based aggregation runs near 820 per second, roughly 60x slower than Aerie.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Ethereum's hash-based post-quantum roadmap carries a large prover-cost disadvantage relative to lattice designs.
insights.locator: We also compared Aerie with leanVM

insights.claim: Lattice signature verification is mostly algebraic with only a handful of hash evaluations, whereas hash-based signatures need hundreds of hashes each, and proving hashes typically adds over 100x overhead versus native computation.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Proving cost, not signature size, is the bottleneck for hash-based post-quantum aggregation.

insights.claim: Falcon's hash takes only message and salt, so including salts in the aggregate lets the verifier compute every hash itself and the proof covers only algebraic checks; for large batches the salts (about 1.3 MB for 32,768) dwarf the 66 KiB proof.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Salt handling is the remaining size lever; deterministic-Falcon chains like Algorand can drop salts entirely.

insights.claim: Aerie's speed comes from Akita, a lattice polynomial commitment scheme built with LayerZero Labs, plus sum-check proving techniques from Lattice Jolt that are highly parallel and GPU-friendly, so more speedup is available.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: GPU acceleration could widen the lead; watch Jolt-family lattice zkVM progress.

insights.claim: Ethereum's plan has each leanVM proof cover only about 900 signatures, requiring sequential rounds of recursive merging; recursion is bug-prone and its security cannot be established even in the random oracle model, whereas Aerie produces one direct proof with no recursion.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Removing recursion frees slot time for vote collection and block propagation and lets more participants aggregate.

insights.claim: Direct single-proof aggregation simplifies failure recovery: if an aggregator fails, any node holding the same signatures can produce a replacement proof.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Reduces liveness risk in proof-of-stake consensus design.

insights.claim: Signature aggregation is what makes large validator sets practical: Ethereum combines tens of thousands of BLS validator signatures per slot, and Solana, where validator votes are about three-quarters of transactions, is adopting BLS aggregation via Alpenglow, yet BLS is not post-quantum.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Both major PoS chains rely on an aggregation primitive that quantum computers would break.

insights.claim: Falcon is easier to deploy than a year ago: fixed-point signing replaces floating point (NIST plans to require this in FN-DSA) and a new implementation cuts Falcon-512 signing to about 11 kB RAM, small enough for hardware-wallet secure elements.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Reduces the main practical objection to Falcon for wallets.

insights.claim: Light SPHINCS- variants take from 47 seconds to over six minutes to sign on a Ledger secure element, so stateless hash-based signatures are also a hardware-wallet challenge.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Hash-only post-quantum account signatures face real wallet UX constraints.

insights.claim: Solana is exploring Falcon and Algorand has deployed it; for chains that choose Falcon, Aerie offers a fast path to aggregation, and the team is extending to ML-DSA and hybrid lattice-plus-elliptic-curve signatures while still expecting headroom over 1,000 per second.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Chains already moving to Falcon are the likely early adopters.

insights.claim: Stateful signatures like XMSS fit the consensus layer, where slot number acts as state, but are dangerous at the execution layer because signing from two devices or restoring a backup can reuse state and enable forgery, which is why Ethereum plans stateless hash-based account signatures.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Explains why Ethereum needs the costlier stateless scheme for accounts.

themes.theme: Lattices vs hash-only security and privacy

insights.claim: Speculative cryptanalytic risk to lattices must be weighed against the present risks of more complicated systems, and relying exclusively on hash-based cryptography may look safer but yields more brittle systems.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Signals a16z crypto will lobby for lattice adoption in Ethereum's roadmap; watch the debate and AI-cryptanalysis speculation.

insights.claim: Ethereum's planned consensus and account signatures are custom schemes outside NIST standards with the hash still undecided, limiting support from hardware wallets, HSMs and institutional custody systems.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Non-standard crypto raises institutional custody integration friction.

insights.claim: The Ethereum Foundation's strawmap lists both a private L1 with shielded transfers and a hash-based post-quantum L1 as north stars, but these conflict because encryption cannot be built from hashes alone (Impagliazzo-Rudich), so any private chain will depend on lattices such as ML-KEM.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Private-payment roadmaps on Ethereum imply lattice dependence regardless of signature choice; hash-only purity is not achievable.
insights.quote: A classic result of Russell Impagliazzo and Steven Rudich shows that public-key encryption cannot be built from hash functions in a black-box way.

insights.claim: Keeping encrypted notes off-chain does not avoid encryption, since notes must still travel encrypted over channels already moving to ML-KEM, and adds an availability dependency, metadata exposure and risk that recipients cannot find and spend funds.
insights.speaker: Alberto Centelles
insights.so_what: Off-chain note delivery is a weaker workaround for private payments than it appears.
